evidence: R-020 promotion — user-auth posture decision and cross-machine evidence
decision: AUTH_MODE=token (boss approved): loopback stays open for the local UI; every off-box request must present COCHPIA_API_TOKEN (Bearer, timing-safe compare). Supabase multi-user (AUTH_MODE=required) remains available when a second real user exists.
enforcement: edge: scripts/core-v0-tls-front.mjs rejects off-box requests without a valid token (401) — the front sees the real client address; behind it every connection is loopback
app: server/auth.js token mode — same rule for direct (non-fronted) deployments; fail-fast startup validation when AUTH_MODE=token without COCHPIA_API_TOKEN
credential domains: the edge accepts either COCHPIA_API_TOKEN or MEMORY_SERVICE_TOKEN; the latter is still fully verified by the /v1 boundary behind the gate (A-09/A-10 unchanged)

runs.check: edge gate, no token, from B machine
app gate direct (0.0.0.0 bind): no token / wrong token / valid token / loopback
full acceptance over TLS+Bearer from B machine

results.detail: legacy and target fixtures share one scenario
target route and idempotency header are present
target turn creates one durable binding, admission, raw event and assistant commit
exact replay returns the original receipt without new canonical facts
conflicting idempotency replay is rejected before external calls
application and Memory session binding keys are unique and immutable
retrieval degradation is explicit and the turn still commits
unknown admission remains pending until the same turn is retried
commit failure leaves no visible assistant success
restart reconciliation reuses the persisted turn and event identifiers
direct Memory event write requires a verified service identity
direct Memory mutation requires producer, correlation and idempotency context
the public Memory governance write surface is gone, so no Core chat-event bypass path exists
the legacy chat path is gone (404) and the target route completes the scenario twice -- JSON and SSE -- with durable checkpoints

honestLimits: single shared credential: no per-user identity, no per-device revocation — matches the personal-instance threat model; revisit when a second real user exists
loopback stays open by design (same trust boundary as the local UI)
token value not archived here; evidence run used a throwaway LAN secret
